messages:
Sam (platform): Heads-up — planning to flip on the new burst_queueing_v2 flag for a scoped canary tomorrow morning. Goal: let short bursts bypass strict queueing for latency-sensitive low‑token requests, but keep strict max_concurrency guardrails.
Maya (runtime): +1. What scope are you thinking for the canary? internal-only or small prod slice?
Sam (platform): Start internal (dev + staging) for 30m smoke, then 2% prod traffic for 2 hours if metrics look good. If latency tail improves and no error spike, widen.
Jon (sre): Need explicit rollback conditions. Suggest: 5xx rate > 0.5% over baseline OR p99 latency regress > 200ms => rollback. Also require SLO alert thresholds enabled.
Li (infra): Do we need any node-level capacity guardrails? If bursts increase immediate GPU utilization we should limit per-pod concurrency. Propose adding `max_concurrency_per_instance: 8` for canary.
Katie (ml): For quality: ensure we route to quantized model variant only if token length < 256. Burst path should avoid lower-quality variants. Also confirm KV-cache hit behavior stays the same.
Sam (platform): Agreed on rollback and per-instance limit. Plan to use: `max_concurrency_per_instance=8`, `queue_timeout_ms=5000`, `burst_token_threshold=256`. Canary audience: `internal:dev,staging; prod:2% by region (us-west-2, eu-west-1)`.
Maya (runtime): Can we also gate by route? Only enable for `generate/text` and not embeddings or admin routes.
Sam (platform): Yes — scope will be route-scoped in feature flag config.
Jon (sre): Add monitoring dashboards: token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, instance GPU utilization. Also set an alert playbook: auto rollback + page on sustained 5xx spike.
Sam (platform): I'll add runbook steps. Quick question: do we need a kill-switch in console for manual immediate disable?
Li (infra): Console kill-switch exists, add a shortcut in the runbook. I can wire an IAM-limited button for SRE on-call only.
Katie (ml): One more: ensure eval harness is run with canary config before prod rollout — I can run the 50-sample prompt set against burst path to check output diffs.
Sam (platform): Perfect. Timeline: tomorrow 09:00 UTC internal smoke for 30m, 10:00 UTC start 2% prod canary for 2h. If green, expand to 20% at 13:00 UTC, then full at 16:00 UTC.
Maya (runtime): I'll prepare the feature-flag manifest. Example CLI toggle: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '\"{\\\"flag\\\":\\\"burst_queueing_v2\\\",\\\"state\\\":\\\"on\\\",\\\"scope\\\":{\\\"routes\\\":[\\\"/v1/generate\\\"],\\\"canary\\\":\\\"2%:us-west-2,eu-west-1\\\"},\\\"guardrails\\\":{\\\"max_concurrency_per_instance\\\":8,\\\"queue_timeout_ms\\\":5000}}\"'`
Sam (platform): Nice. Can someone review the manifest before I schedule the toggle?
Jon (sre): I'll review monitoring hooks.
Li (infra): I'll review IAM + kill-switch.
Katie (ml): I'll run the evals after you flip internal. Ping me when internal smoke starts.
deploy-bot: staging deploy completed: service/runner v3.14.1 -> OK (2025-09-01T08:59:12Z).
ops-bot: Feature flag draft created: burst_queueing_v2, id=f-9a8b. Access the flag editor: https://console.redwood/flags/f-9a8b
Sam (platform): Thanks — tagging the runbook link and checklist in ops: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/burst_queueing_v2_checklist. I'll schedule the toggle and post an update 15m before start.
Maya (runtime): SGTM. I'll push the manifest to the infra repo and open a tiny PR for traceability.
Jon (sre): Quick nit: include a synthetic traffic job with traffic shape matching tail calls. I can provide a k8s job yaml.
Sam (platform): Excellent — adding that. If no objections by EOD I'll proceed with scheduling. :thumbsup:
Li (infra): No objections from infra.
Katie (ml): All good from ML.
Maya (runtime): Merged the manifest PR, link: https://git.redwood/infra/feature-flags/merge/321
Sam (platform): Closing loop — scheduled internal smoke 2025-09-02 09:00 UTC. Will ping here when it starts.
Jon (sre): Will be on-call during canary window.
Sam (platform): Thanks everyone.
